answer: With 120 s allowed lateness the watermark is the largest event time minus 120, so after event e (time 130) it is 10, not 100. Window 0 (ends at 60) is still open when event g (time 20, arrives 140) comes in, so g is no longer dropped. Window 0 then totals 24 (15 + 9) and closes once event f (time 200) moves the watermark to 80. Window 60 stays open because the watermark has only reached 80 and its end is 120. The output would be {0: 24.0, ...} with window 60 still open, instead of window 0 at 15 with g dropped.
